summary: 200 OK · 77B markdown · stealthy · this call makes 1 extra direct request to the target before the browser runs: a liveness probe (direct, 3s, no retries, no synthetic headers, no redirect hop). Your service's own log will show that one next to the browser's navigation - it is dhole dialing, not the page. · pin=true could not be honored: an anonymous auto session is shared between callers and is recycled when idle, so there is no page of yours to keep open. Name a session_id= (the one you use for logins) and pass pin=true again. · the target is loopback/private, so the browser tier navigated without dhole's invented google referer. What that browser sends of its own (UA, `sec-ch-ua*`, `sec-fetch-*`) arrived as it always does, plus every header you named · bot_wall_detected: page is an anti-bot/CAPTCHA challenge, not content · 1 action(s) waiting for user approval (click '#captcha-btn')
next_action: a submit action is PAUSED for user approval (pending_approval in metadata.actions) - describe the submission to the user and ask for confirmation; on a yes, re-run the same actions with {"confirm": true} on that submit. Nothing irreversible was done.

diagnosis.recover_with: the action chain ran — `metadata.actions` holds one receipt per step, and that is the answer about this call. The content verdict describes the page it left behind, not the chain. Do NOT re-issue the same chain: every step already marked ok would run again (a fill would fill twice).
